subject: How can I trim off left and right gully areas? [SEC=UNCLASSIFIED]

messages.author: 5c54e507aaca9ede
messages.subject: How can I trim off left and right gully areas? [SEC=UNCLASSIFIED]
parts:
Hi,

The data I am plotting represents Latitudes (-90 to +90 degrees)
across the X-axis, and "ggplot" seems to display what I am
calling a "gully" area on the left and right sides of the
plot (See the example in attached PDF file "z-wv-c.pdf").

I'd like to be able to trim that away, or expand the plot
so that the X-axis is -90., through 0., through +90.,
with no extra graph plot area on each side.
Can that be done? Any pointer on how to achieve that
would be really appreciated.

The 'R' code used to produce the attached plot is:

library(ggplot2)
#
# WvTr <- read.table("Wv-tr.dat", header=T)
# Example-Data:
# X x90sinX Y Y.lo Y.up
# 88.750000 89.978582 0.629233 0.534234 0.724233
# 86.250000 89.807303 0.576637 0.486925 0.666350
# 83.750000 89.465070 0.616868 0.532442 0.701294
# ...
#
p1 <- ggplot(data=WvTr,
aes(x=x90sinX, y=Y,
ymin=Y.lo, ymax=Y.up,
fill=type, linetype=type)) +
theme_bw() +
opts(panel.grid.minor=theme_blank()) +
xlim(-90, 90) +
opts(title = "(a) Transient") +
opts(legend.position = "none") +
geom_line(size=1) +
geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0.0)) +
geom_ribbon(alpha=0.5) +
xlab(xlabel) +
ylab(ylabel) +
scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(-90,-77.94,-45,0,45,77.94,90),
labels = c(-90,-60,-30,0,30,60,90))
ggsave(p1, file="z-wv-a.pdf", width=8, height=4.5)

In addition to trimming off the left and right gullies,
I'd also like to have darker lines for the axes
(left, right, top, and bottom), and to increase
the font size for the axes labels.

Best regards,

> In addition to trimming off the left and right gullies,
> I'd also like to have darker lines for the axes
> (left, right, top, and bottom), and to increase
> the font size for the axes labels.

For this you want to alter the theme, run theme_bw() to see what you should change, but you probably want something like:

opts(panel.background=theme_rect(colour="black"), axis.x.text=theme_text(size=12), axis.y.text=theme_text(size=12))
